pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks the seeded rows are all 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
The item() helper in src/index.js prefixes ★. 'AC-2' asserts the exact list [First item, ★ Second item, Third item].
The starred view adds WHERE starred = 1 with ORDER BY id. 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and expects them in id order.
'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all both list every item in id order, with the starred one marked.
'AC-5' asserts the 'Starred only' link on / and the 'All items' link on /?show=starred.
Object.hasOwn(VIEWS, show) gates the view, and anything else returns 400. 'AC-6' covers Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__, checking status 400 and no <li>.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. 'AC-7' asserts it. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts the query form, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers it.

findings.what: AC-1 says 'every existing item starts unstarred'. The test only checks freshly seeded rows after all migrations run. It does not insert rows before 0002 and then migrate them.
findings.fix: Optional: apply 0001, insert rows, apply 0002, then assert starred = 0.

findings.what: The README mentions the ?show=starred view but not the ★ marker, the show=all value, or the 400 on other values.
findings.fix: Add one short clause covering them.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The change implements it, and the starred-items spec file has no later edits after the go.
All 7 acceptance items and all 4 state-table rows have named tests. The decisions are followed: id order is kept and the view is a query parameter.

I could not run the tests here because vitest is not installed, so 'npm test' failed with 'vitest: not found'. .github/workflows/ci.yml exists, so CI runs them. I read the tests and each would fail if its behaviour broke. The traffic fake-app change is a tightening, not a loosening.
The README is updated. Only the low-severity gaps above remain.
Object.hasOwn guards the view lookup. The title is HTML-escaped. The SQL is static. I found no defects.
The only user input is the show parameter, which is allow-listed. The query-string regex relaxation in the route checker is limited to a build-time config check.
The diff changes src/index.js server-rendered HTML but adds no UI component, style or template files. No browser evidence was claimed.
The diff has no UI flow beyond two plain links. The tests cover them.
The title and body match the diff: the 400 behaviour, the migration, the routes.json entry, the traffic checker change and the test fake-app change. 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' is true.
